samples.summary: REST insert/delete still leaves merges straddling the freeze — the new invariant's remaining door
samples.evidence: The change establishes "no merged block may straddle a frozen boundary" and closes the editor paths (`Sheet.moveCells`, `moveRangeTo`, `planPasteMerges`) plus, on the API, `POST .../move` (`assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze`) and `PUT .../merges` / `PUT .../freeze`. `Sheet.shiftCells` additionally snaps the boundary after an insert/delete (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1415-1429). The backend's shared insert/delete path does not: `applyShift` at packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:322-360 calls `applyWorksheetShift` and nothing else — the helper adjusts `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:246-265) but never runs `snapFreezePastMerges` or `crossesFreezePane`. So `POST .../insert` (or `delete`) on a tab with a frozen band and a merged block below/inside it can still persist the exact straddling, unpaintable state the rest of the change works to make unreachable, and the engine only repairs it if a later local `shiftCells` happens to run (`loadMerges`/`loadFreezePane` do not snap — see the test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:835 which seeds precisely this state). Fix belongs in `applyShift` (or inside `applyWorksheetShift`, which would also cover the frontend store path).

samples.summary: `applyWorksheetShift`'s doc comment now describes a contract Sheet no longer honours
samples.evidence: The comment at packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:178-182 justifies applying the freeze adjustment in both places because "`Sheet` persists these fields by assigning the whole value it computed from its own in-memory state ... so the editor's later write is the same value again." After this change `Sheet.shiftCells` runs `snapFreezePastMerges` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1415-1429) and can write a *different*, larger freeze than the one `applyWorksheetShift` just stored, so the stated equivalence no longer holds and the helper is now silently the weaker of the two.

samples.summary: Freeze-handle drag now gets a boundary different from the one it dragged to
samples.evidence: `handleFreezeHandleDrag`-style code at packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:2972-2977 (and the double-click quick-freeze at :1384-1392) calls `this.setFreezePane(targetIndex, ...)` and assumes the boundary lands on `targetIndex`. `Sheet.setFreezePane` now snaps past any merged block the index would cut, so the drag can jump the line well below/right of the pointer and a drag back above the block cannot reduce it. The view re-reads `getFreezePane()` so nothing breaks, but the drag interaction is now out of step with what the handler requested — worth a deliberate look at the handle's preview/drag state.

samples.summary: Copy marching-ants overlay now persists after a paste, since the view no longer clears the buffer
samples.evidence: The render path at packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:5614 passes `this.sheet!.getCopyRange()` / `isCutMode()` to the overlay's copy-range border (packages/sheets/src/view/overlay.ts:775-822). With the `clearCopyBuffer()` calls removed from `Worksheet.paste` (worksheet.ts:4953) and `Spreadsheet.paste` (spreadsheet.ts:728), a copy's dashed border now stays on screen after the first paste until Escape (worksheet.ts:5123). That is the stated intent, but it is a visible behaviour change in an out-of-diff render path and may move baselines in the browser visual lane (packages/frontend/src/app/harness/visual/sheet-scenarios.tsx).

samples.summary: REST API doc does not record the new freeze-snap response or the merges 409
samples.evidence: `PUT .../freeze` may now answer with a larger boundary than requested and `PUT .../merges` may now answer 409, but docs/design/rest-api.md's worksheet section (only line 286 mentions the freeze pane, in passing) still describes the endpoints as plain field replacements. Downstream consumers that echo the response — e.g. the CLI's `sheets freeze set` / `merges set` (packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-view.ts:105-141, :258-300) and packages/cli/README.md:158 — carry no note of either new outcome.

finding.summary: REST insert/delete still leaves merges straddling the freeze — the new invariant's remaining door
finding.evidence: The change establishes "no merged block may straddle a frozen boundary" and closes the editor paths (`Sheet.moveCells`, `moveRangeTo`, `planPasteMerges`) plus, on the API, `POST .../move` (`assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze`) and `PUT .../merges` / `PUT .../freeze`. `Sheet.shiftCells` additionally snaps the boundary after an insert/delete (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1415-1429). The backend's shared insert/delete path does not: `applyShift` at packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:322-360 calls `applyWorksheetShift` and nothing else — the helper adjusts `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:246-265) but never runs `snapFreezePastMerges` or `crossesFreezePane`. So `POST .../insert` (or `delete`) on a tab with a frozen band and a merged block below/inside it can still persist the exact straddling, unpaintable state the rest of the change works to make unreachable, and the engine only repairs it if a later local `shiftCells` happens to run (`loadMerges`/`loadFreezePane` do not snap — see the test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:835 which seeds precisely this state). Fix belongs in `applyShift` (or inside `applyWorksheetShift`, which would also cover the frontend store path).

verdict.reason: The snap call really is absent from `applyShift`/`applyWorksheetShift`, but the claimed consequence cannot occur. The freeze adjustment in `shiftWorksheetViewState` (worksheet-structure.ts:249-265) and the merge remap in `shiftMergeAxis` (merging.ts:31-60) apply the same (index, count) arithmetic, so they move in lockstep and the "no merge straddles the boundary" invariant is preserved by construction for every branch. Insert: if i<=f the boundary grows by c and any merge with a>f necessarily has i<=a so it shifts by the same c; a merge with b<=f either shifts wholly or grows to b+c<=f+c. Delete: f'=f-min(c,f-i+1); for b<=f, j<=f implies c<=f-i+1 so b'<=f'; for a>f, a clipped head implies j>f hence c>f-i+1 hence f'=i-1 while a'=i. The repo's own tests confirm this reading: merge.test.ts:815-831 asserts an insert inside the frozen band keeps the block whole with "no snapping needed", while the snap-after-insert tests (merge.test.ts:833-858, 860-874) must inject the straddling merge directly into the store, and their comment states it is a state this replica cannot create and that arrives from a peer. The shiftCells snap is repair of externally-seeded corruption, not a guard the REST shift path can bypass; the doors that could write such a state are guarded (worksheet.controller.ts:112-119 snaps freeze, :184-200 refuses merges 409, worksheet-structure.controller.ts:173-196 refuses moves). Failing to repair a pre-existing peer-written violation is not a guard bypass and is not blocking under the blast-radius rubric.

finding.summary: Row/column drag-reorder re-selects the drop position even when the move was refused. `moveRows`/`moveColumns` now return void after an early `merge-move-frozen` refusal, but this caller unconditionally runs `selectRow(newStart)` / `selectColumnRange(...)` in the `.then()` and re-renders, so the user sees the selection jump to the destination while the rows never moved. The move APIs give callers no success signal, so this site cannot distinguish refusal from success.
finding.evidence: packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4656-4676 — `movePromise.then(() => { const newStart = ...; this.sheet!.selectRow(newStart); ... this.render(); })` with no check that the move actually happened; the refusal is added at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1552-1562.

verdict.reason: The finding describes code that does not exist as stated. It claims `moveRows`/`moveColumns` "now return void after an early merge-move-frozen refusal" and that the drag-reorder caller "unconditionally runs selectRow(newStart)/selectColumnRange(...) in the .then()". Both are false in the working tree. `sheet.ts:1316` and `sheet.ts:1324` are declared `Promise<boolean>`, delegating to `moveCells` (`sheet.ts:1527-1533`, also `Promise<boolean>`), which returns `false` at every refusal — no-op destination (1536-1538), merge-split (1542-1544), and the `merge-move-frozen` refusal the finding cites (1552-1558) — and `true` only on write paths (1616, 1629). At the caller, `worksheet.ts:4661` destructures the signal (`movePromise.then((moved) => {`) and `worksheet.ts:4666` performs an explicit `if (!moved) return;` guard that precedes all selection calls and `this.render()` at 4669-4681. So a refused move cannot re-select the drop position, and the claim that "the move APIs give callers no success signal" is contradicted by the boolean return. I also ran the blast-radius grep for every other reference to the changed contract: the only non-test call sites are worksheet.ts:4658-4659 (guarded); the rest are tests that ignore the return value harmlessly (moving.test.ts, formatting.test.ts, test/helpers/concurrency-driver.ts:52,55), one test that asserts the boolean directly (merge.test.ts:1112-1113), and docs already describing the refusal contract (docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:167). No caller is left on the old shape.

mergedFrom.summary: `sortFilterByColumn` rewrites cells to new row positions (deleteRange + setGrid with remapped rows) but does not call `clearCopyBuffer`, unlike the newly-updated `shiftCells` and `moveCells`. Since the buffer now persists across pastes, a copy → filter-sort → paste relocates from coordinates whose contents moved.

finding.summary: `undo`/`redo` renumber cells (they replay structural ops such as row insert/delete/move) and reload merges, dimensions and freeze state, but never call `clearCopyBuffer`. The diff establishes the invariant that every edit renumbering the snapshotted cells must drop the buffer, and makes the buffer outlive the paste, so a copy → structural edit → undo → paste now relocates values AND re-creates merged blocks from stale coordinates.
finding.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:5306-5333 (`undo`) and 5338-5360 (`redo`) call `loadDimensions/loadStyles/loadMerges/loadFreezePane/...` with no `clearCopyBuffer()`; the invariant is stated at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2217-2221.

verdict.reason: The claimed absence does not exist. `Sheet.undo()` (sheet.ts:5355) calls `this.clearCopyBuffer()` at sheet.ts:5365 and `Sheet.redo()` (sheet.ts:5394) calls it at sheet.ts:5399, in both cases before `loadDimensions/loadStyles/loadMerges/loadFreezePane/loadHiddenState/loadFilterState/loadPivotDefinition`. The comments at 5359-5364 and 5398 state exactly the rationale the reviewer says is missing (an undone/redone step may be an insert/delete/reorder that renumbers the snapshotted cells, so the buffer is dropped either way to prevent a later paste relocating values and re-creating merged blocks from stale coordinates). The reviewer's cited evidence range (5306-5333) is not `undo` at all — it is the row/range style-removal loop of an unrelated method. A grep for `async (undo|redo)\(` in that file returns only these two definitions, so there is no second undo/redo path lacking the call, and the invariant doc at 2217-2222 explicitly lists `undo`/`redo` as callers, consistent with the code. The copy → structural edit → undo → paste scenario is already guarded.

finding.summary: The remote-change path (`Worksheet.reloadDimensions`, driven from `sheet-view.tsx`'s remote sync) reloads dimensions, merges, freeze and hidden state after another peer's structural edit, but does not clear the copy buffer. Because the buffer now survives pastes indefinitely, a local paste after a remote row/column insert or reorder relocates from stale coordinates and re-creates merged blocks at the wrong place.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `Worksheet.reloadDimensions` (the remote-sync path) does not clear the copy buffer after a peer's structural edit. It does — via a differently-named helper, which is why the reviewer's `grep clearCopyBuffer` missed it. `packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:5248` calls `this.sheet!.revalidateCopyBuffer()` inside `reloadDimensions` (which spans 5230-5261, not the 5224-5247 cited), sitting between `resolveAnchorsToRefs()` at 5240 and the hidden-state resync at 5250 — inside the very block reported as lacking it. `Sheet.revalidateCopyBuffer` (sheet.ts:2259-2275) resolves the buffer's recorded `sourceAnchors` against the current row/col order and calls `clearCopyBuffer()` at 2273 when the axis IDs no longer sit at the recorded indices; `copy()` populates `sourceAnchors` at sheet.ts:2290, so the required data is captured. The full chain the finding names holds: sheet-view.tsx:1181-1182 `runRemoteSync` -> `reloadDimensions()` -> worksheet.ts:5248 -> sheet.ts:2273. The exact described scenario is covered by merge.test.ts:1151-1184, where a peer row insert renumbering 'r2' drops the buffer while a peer cell edit leaves it intact. No reload entry point bypasses this: spreadsheet.ts:103-105 merely delegates to worksheet.reloadDimensions(), and all other callers funnel through the same method. A separate correctness-lens concern about the early return when `sourceAnchors` is undefined (sheet.ts:2261) is logic inside the new code, out of the blast-radius lane, and does not restore this absence claim.

finding.summary: The server-side axis move endpoint mirrors only the 'move would split a merged block' refusal; it has no equivalent of the new `merge-move-frozen` check that `Sheet.moveCells` now enforces. An API `POST move` can therefore land a merged block across a frozen row/column, producing exactly the state the renderer cannot paint (a block spanning the frozen pane and the scrolling body) and that the editor refuses to create.
finding.evidence: packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:135-153 `assertMoveKeepsMerges` checks only `isMergeSplitByMove`; the move handler is at :218-260. The new client-side guard is packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1547-1558.

verdict.reason: The backend move endpoint does have the frozen-pane equivalent of `merge-move-frozen`. `packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:173-196` defines `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze`, which reads `ws.frozenRows`/`ws.frozenCols`, computes the post-move merge map with `moveMergeMap(merges, axis, srcIndex, count, dstIndex)` (line 185), and throws a `ConflictException` for any resulting merge where `crossesFreezePane(range, frozenRows, frozenCols)` is true (lines 187-194). It is actually wired into the `@Post('move')` handler at line 287-293, immediately after `assertMoveKeepsMerges` (line 286) and before `applyWorksheetMove` (line 294), so it runs inside `doc.update` prior to any mutation. This mirrors the client guard at `packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1552-1555` (`moveMergeMap` + `crossesFreezePane(toMergeRange(...))` -> `refuse('merge-move-frozen')`) using the same shared helpers exported from `packages/sheets/src/index.ts:126,128`. The reviewer's claim that grep for `moveMergeMap` and for `frozen` in this controller came up empty is contradicted by lines 13, 18, 180-188. A backend spec also covers this case at `packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts:402`. The API is therefore not an unguarded door into a straddling merged block.

finding.summary: `PUT freeze` writes `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` straight into the document with no equivalent of the new `snapFreezePastMerges` step, so an API client can set a freeze boundary that cuts an existing merged block in half — the undrawable state `setFreezePane` was just changed to avoid. The same hole exists for the merges settings write (:146), which validates span size but not freeze straddling.
finding.evidence: packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet.controller.ts:68-77 — `ws.frozenRows = rows; ws.frozenCols = cols;` with no merge snapping; the new model-side snap is packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:519-548.

verdict.reason: The claimed absence is present in the exact file cited. `PUT freeze` calls the shared `snapFreezePastMerges` (imported at worksheet.controller.ts:15) inside `doc.update` at lines 112-116 and stores the snapped values at 117-119, returning the adjusted boundary — the same helper `Sheet.setFreezePane` uses (sheet.ts:533, 546-550, implemented in merging.ts:207). The second half of the finding is also wrong: `PUT merges` calls `assertMergesClearOfFreeze` at lines 244-248 before writing `ws.merges` at 249, and that helper (184-200) uses `toMergeRange`/`crossesFreezePane` to throw a 409 when a block would straddle the freeze. The reviewer's quoted evidence (`ws.frozenRows = rows; ws.frozenCols = cols;` at :68-77) does not exist in the file; lines 68-87 are the GET handler.
